samples.summary: Both view paste paths call `clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally right after `sheet.paste(...)`, so the new merge propagation only ever runs on the FIRST paste after a copy
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4937-4938 `await this.sheet!.paste({ text, html }); this.sheet!.clearCopyBuffer();` and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:724-725 do the same. `Sheet.paste` only takes the internal branch when `this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2233). Once the view has cleared the buffer, a second Ctrl+V of the same clipboard content falls through to the plain-TSV branch (sheet.ts:2290), which carries no merges and is explicitly exempt from the new plan/refuse logic. The user-visible consequence is precisely the bug this change fixes: the 2nd and later pastes re-introduce the 'values written into cells hidden under a destination merge, resurfacing on unmerge' behaviour, and `merge-paste-partial` never fires. The new unit tests drive `Sheet` directly and never call `clearCopyBuffer`, so nothing in the suite covers the real app sequence. Fix likely belongs at the two view call sites (only clear on cut, or clear only when the paste actually consumed the buffer).

samples.summary: A refused `merge-paste-partial` paste still loses the user's cut/copy buffer, because the view clears it unconditionally after `paste()` returns
samples.evidence: New early return at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2260-2263 leaves `copyBuffer` intact, but packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4938 and packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:725 call `clearCopyBuffer()` regardless of outcome. After the toast ('Unmerge the destination first'), the user cannot simply unmerge and press Ctrl+V again — the marching ants / cut state are gone and they must re-copy. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260912-sheets-paste-merge-propagation-todo.md:45-49) acknowledges this, but it is still an out-of-diff call site that degrades the new refusal's UX.

samples.summary: Merges created by `applyPasteMerges` bypass `canMergeSelection`'s frozen-pane constraint, which every interactive merge path honours
samples.evidence: `canMergeSelection` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4602-4610) refuses any merge that crosses a frozen row/column boundary, and `mergeSelection` is gated on it (sheet.ts:4629). `applyPasteMerges` calls `this.store.setMerge(merge.anchor, merge.span)` (sheet.ts:2483) with no such check, so copying a merged block and pasting it so it straddles `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` produces a merge the merge UI would have rejected; the renderer draws frozen and unfrozen quadrants separately (packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:260-415), so such a block renders inconsistently across the freeze split. Note `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2698-2712) already has the same gap, so this is a widening of an existing hole rather than a brand-new one.

samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` now makes `activeCell` and `ranges[0][0]` the SAME object, where they used to be distinct literals
samples.evidence: New code: `this.activeCell = from; this.ranges = [[from, to]];` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2561-2563) — `from` is the single `Ref` returned by `rangeOf`. Previously each was a freshly constructed `{r,c}`. Any consumer that mutates a range endpoint in place would now silently move the active cell too. `getRanges()`/`getRange()` hand out the internal arrays without cloning (sheet.ts:3314-3325), so an external mutator is possible; I found no current in-place mutator of a live `this.ranges` entry (`resizeRange` at sheet.ts:4033 and `moveToEdge` at sheet.ts:3920 both clone first), which is why confidence is low. Cheap fix: clone in `selectPastedRange`.

samples.summary: `planPasteMerges` translates merge anchors/spans with no `dimensionRange` bound, so a paste near the grid edge can create a block extending past the grid
samples.evidence: `planPasteMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2415-2420) builds `destRange`/`pasted` purely by adding the delta; nothing checks `isRangeInRange(destRange, this.dimensionRange)` the way `resizeRange` does (sheet.ts:4084). Merges created interactively cannot leave the grid because the selection cannot. The backend validator treats in-grid merge geometry as an invariant worth restating (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:10-23, 107-130) and `rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:816) will then map covered srefs that lie outside the grid. Low confidence because spans are bounded by the copied block and `moveRangeTo` has the same gap.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. view/worksheet.ts:4937-4938 and view/spreadsheet.ts:724-725 both call `this.sheet.clearCopyBuffer()` unconditionally on the line immediately after `await sheet.paste({text, html})` — no cut-only condition, no check that the buffer was consumed. sheet.ts:2138-2140 shows clearCopyBuffer sets copyBuffer = undefined, and only copy() (2153) / cut() (2174) repopulate it; paste() never does. sheet.ts:2233 gates the internal branch on `this.copyBuffer && text === this.copyBuffer.text`, and the entire new merge feature — planPasteMerges (2248), the `merge-paste-partial` refusal (2260-2263), pastedMerges/replacedMerges (2264-2265) — is inside that branch. The HTML (2286) and plain-TSV (2290-2293) branches leave pastedMerges/replacedMerges at their empty initial values (2226-2231), making applyPasteMerges (2330) a no-op. Therefore a second Ctrl+V of the same clipboard content after the view has cleared the buffer falls to string2grid (2292) and silently reintroduces the exact "values hidden under a destination merge" behaviour the change was written to fix, with the refusal never firing. This is a blast-radius finding by construction: the nullifying call sites are outside the diff, and the new tests exercise Sheet directly without the view's clear. No guard elsewhere restores the buffer, so `already-guarded` does not apply; the code is present verbatim, so `not-present` does not apply; and a consumer outside the diff defeating the diff's new contract is precisely this lens's lane, so `out-of-scope` does not apply.

finding.summary: Split-refusal is now suppressed based on a stale copy-buffer snapshot; nothing invalidates copyBuffer.merges between cut and paste
finding.evidence: The new `travelling` set is built from `this.copyBuffer.merges` (sheet.ts:2431-2437), a snapshot taken at cut time. `copyBuffer` is only ever cleared explicitly (sheet.ts:2138-2140, 2284) — `unmergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4679-4713), `mergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4658) and the row/column structural ops (sheet.ts:1245, 1253) never invalidate or re-map it. So after a cut, a user (or a remote collaborator over yorkie-store) can unmerge/re-merge so that a block currently anchored at a stale source anchor spans into the destination region; that block is then excluded from the `isRangeInRange` split check even though it is a live destination block, and it is instead deleted wholesale by the cut branch's `replacedMerges` push (sheet.ts:2276-2282) using the stale span. A refusal the guard is supposed to raise is skipped and a destination block disappears silently. To confirm: exercise cut → unmerge/merge at the same anchor with a wider span → paste at an overlapping destination. Fix belongs on the new code (validate travelling anchors against the current merge map, or invalidate the copy buffer on merge-map changes).

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `planPasteMerges` builds `travelling` from the copy-buffer snapshot (sheet.ts:2432-2434, fed by this.copyBuffer.merges at sheet.ts:2250) and uses it to exclude those anchors from the split-refusal check (sheet.ts:2435-2440). The buffer is only ever cleared at sheet.ts:2139, sheet.ts:2284, and the view-level post-paste/Escape sites (view/worksheet.ts:4938, view/worksheet.ts:5109, view/spreadsheet.ts:725); a full grep for `copyBuffer` shows no other writers. The merge-map mutators mergeSelection (sheet.ts:4658-4660), unmergeSelection (sheet.ts:4697-4700) and shiftCells-based row/column ops (sheet.ts:1245-1272) never invalidate or re-map it, and both merge paths are UI-reachable while a cut buffer is live (view/spreadsheet.ts:563-565, view/worksheet.ts:5180). The cut branch then pushes the stale spans into replacedMerges (sheet.ts:2276-2282) and applyPasteMerges deletes by anchor with no existence/span validation (sheet.ts:2471-2480), so a live destination block anchored at a stale source anchor escapes the refusal and is silently removed. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable; it is an invariant assumed by the new code and violated by unchanged sites, which is in this lens's lane.

finding.summary: Paste-created merges bypass the freeze-pane guard that every other merge-creation path honours, violating the invariant documented at docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253 and assumed by the renderer
finding.evidence: The only existing merge-creation entry point, `mergeSelection`, refuses a block crossing the freeze boundary via `canMergeSelection` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4591-4599: `crossesFrozenRows`/`crossesFrozenCols`). `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253` states "Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed." The new `planPasteMerges` (sheet.ts:2390) translates the copied blocks by the paste delta and creates them with no freeze check, so with `frozenCols=2` copying a merged D1:E1 and pasting at B1 yields a B1:C1 block straddling the boundary. The renderer relies on the invariant: `packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1917` `toCellRect` computes the merged rect from a single scrolled origin, so a straddling block is drawn with the wrong rect across the frozen pane (the same hole exists in `moveRangeTo`, which is also unguarded, but this change adds a second reachable path). Fix belongs in `planPasteMerges`/`applyPasteMerges`.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repository. The freeze-pane guard exists exactly as described (sheet.ts:4602-4610, enforced via mergeSelection's gate at sheet.ts:4629) and the invariant is documented at docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:253. The new paste merge path does bypass it: planPasteMerges translates copied blocks by the paste delta at sheet.ts:2415-2418 with no frozenRows/frozenCols reference (its only refusal is the partial-overwrite case at sheet.ts:2438-2440), and applyPasteMerges writes them unconditionally via store.setMerge at sheet.ts:2482-2484. The path is reachable from the public paste() entry point (sheet.ts:2248 and sheet.ts:2330); the only early returns before it are pivotDefinition (sheet.ts:2215) and merge-paste-partial (sheet.ts:2260-2263), so no existing guard makes it unreachable. A grep for frozenRows|frozenCols in sheet.ts shows no occurrence anywhere in the paste path. The renderer consumer assumption also holds: gridcanvas.ts:1917-1939 toCellRect derives both merged-block corners from one scroll origin and is used by the real draw calls (gridcanvas.ts:967, 1043, 1121, 1513) and overlay.ts:575, 684; overlay.ts:1238-1241 documents a separate toCellRectWithFreeze precisely because plain toCellRect is not freeze-aware, so a straddling block renders with a wrong rect. This sits squarely in the blast-radius lane (an invariant another module relies on, violated by a new creation path / a guard with a reachable bypass) and is blocking at major severity.
